# Type workshop

> Adjusts a font's tracking (letter spacing), horizontal width, and variable axis locations, then exports a static TTF or OTF with new family and style names. Accepts TTF, OTF, WOFF, and WOFF2 with TrueType or CFF outlines. CFF2 is unsupported.

Pick one route. Both run the same engine, so the same settings produce the same advances and outlines. The page uses fontTools 4.51, which can round recalculated composite-glyph bounds one unit differently from newer fontTools releases.

- **Command line.** Use this when you have a shell and Python 3. Font files never touch a browser.
- **This page.** Use this when you can only drive a browser. It processes fonts in the page with Pyodide and uploads nothing.

## Settings

The command line and the page accept the same settings and ranges.

| Setting | Range | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tracking | -0.1 to 0.2 em | Rounded half up to 0.001 em. Added to every non-zero advance. Zero-width marks stay at zero. |
| stretch | 50 to 200 percent | Synthetic. Only for fonts without a `wdth` axis. |
| axes | each axis's own min to max | `wdth` replaces stretch when the font has one. Unset axes stay at their defaults. |
| family, style | non-empty text | Defaults: source family + " Workshop", source style. |

Inspect a font first to get its axes and the ranges that apply to it.

## Command line

Download [workshop.py](workshop.py) and [engine.py](engine.py) into one directory. Install `fonttools` and `brotli` with pip.

```sh
python3 workshop.py inspect Font.ttf --json
python3 workshop.py adjust Font.ttf --tracking 0.05 --stretch 120 -o Font-Wide.ttf --json
python3 workshop.py adjust Variable.ttf --axis wght=700 --family "My Sans" --json
```

With `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON object. Success returns the output path, format, `@font-face` CSS, and the settings applied: rounded tracking, stretch (`null` for fonts with a `wdth` axis), and every axis location. Font and adjustment failures return `{"error": "..."}` with exit status 1. Invalid arguments exit 2 and print usage text to stderr, not JSON. `adjust` refuses to overwrite a file unless you pass `--force`. Run `python3 workshop.py adjust --help` for every flag.

## Browser page

Wait for the page to load, then call `window.typeWorkshop` from page scripts. `load`, `adjust`, and `reset` return a promise that resolves with a state report once the export is ready, or rejects with the page's error message. `state()` and `getExport()` return immediately.

```js
await typeWorkshop.load('https://example.com/Font.woff2'); // or a File, Blob, ArrayBuffer or Uint8Array, plus an optional name
const report = await typeWorkshop.adjust({tracking: 0.05, stretch: 120, family: 'My Sans', filename: 'my-sans'});
report.font.axes;      // [{tag, min, max, default}]
report.export.css;     // @font-face CSS
const {data, filename, format} = typeWorkshop.getExport(); // data is a Uint8Array of the font file
```

`adjust` takes any subset of `tracking`, `stretch`, `axes` (an object of tag to value), `family`, `style`, and `filename`. Omitted settings keep their current values. It rejects unknown names, wrong types, and out-of-range values before changing anything. If you call `adjust` again before the first call settles, both settle with the final export. `reset()` restores the default tracking, width, and axes but keeps the names. Fetching a font by URL needs that server to allow cross-origin requests. A URL without a font extension still loads.

The first load downloads Pyodide and fontTools from jsDelivr. Allow up to two minutes before treating it as a failure.

### Driving the controls directly

The `data-state` attribute on `<html>` holds the page status: `empty`, `loading`, `generating`, `ready`, or `error`. `#status` holds the readable message. Wait for `ready` or `error` after every change.

| Control | Selector | How to set it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Font file | `#file` | Set the file input's files |
| Tracking | `#tracking` | Range input in em. Set `value`, then dispatch `input` |
| Stretch or width | `#width` | Range input. Percent for stretch, axis units when the font has `wdth` |
| Other axes | `[data-axis="wght"]` | Range input per axis. Set `value`, then dispatch `input` |
| Family, style, filename | `#family`, `#style`, `#filename` | Text inputs. Dispatch `input` after setting |
| Download | `#download` | Enabled only in the `ready` state |
| CSS | `#css`, `#copy` | `#css` holds the `@font-face` rule |

## Limits

- Synthetic stretch scales outlines and removes TrueType hinting. It thickens or thins vertical strokes.
- GPOS kerning values keep their original size.
- Variable fonts export as a single static instance.
- Modifying and redistributing a font may need permission under its license.
